correctness.rationale: Inversion gives y_{t+1}=a y_t+(1−a)K_t⁻¹ and an attracting positive fixed point of the four-step map, whose slope is a⁴. In coordinates z=(y−c)/d, the cyclic respective solutions starting just before a high season are (D,−D,D,−D) and (B,−E,−B,E); substitution directly checks each update. The sorted partial-sum differences are d(B−D), d(B+E−2D), d(B−D). The first factor difference has numerator 2a(1−a), the second 2a(1−a)², both with denominator (1+a)(1+a²). All are strictly positive. Equality of total reciprocal sums gives the common harmonic mean 1/c; strict Karamata for reciprocal, and comparison of the extrema, give all population consequences. The variance in reciprocal coordinates is D²d² versus (B²+E²)d²/2, giving the ratio (1+a)²/(1+a²). The six labeled schedules split into the alternating orbit of size two and the clustered orbit of size four.
residual_risks: The supplied rational cases do not prove the universal claim. The convex order and variance identity are specifically for inverse abundance.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For the exact prior spectra center at (1+r+r²+r³)/2. The grouped absolute deviations are (r−1)(r+1)²/2 and (r−1)²(r+1)/2, each twice. The alternating absolute deviation is (r−1)(r²+1)/2 four times. The common affine scale cancels in the variance ratio, leaving (r+1)²/(r²+1), the frozen formula. No additional comparison lemma is needed.

value.rationale: The mean-versus-bottleneck tradeoff is intrinsically meaningful, but the distinct catalogue finding gives that exact tradeoff in its stronger convex-order form and supplies the full spectra. The added harmonic-mean language is equivalent to the common reciprocal sum; the variance ratio is immediate central-moment arithmetic on the known spectra and does not survive as a separate valuable finding.
